summary: Updates BCP 101 to tell the IETF Administrative Oversight Committee to set more practical start and end dates for member terms, since the original dates were found impractical. It was replaced by RFC 8711.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7691 updates the rules for when IAOC member terms begin and end. It lets the IAOC set dates around a regular meeting near the first IETF meeting of the year and requires chair selection as the first order of business.

subtitle: Updates the timing rules for IAOC member terms and chair selection.

tldr.problem: BCP 101's term end dates made it difficult for the IAOC and IETF Trust to conduct business and select chairs during the first IETF meeting week.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7691 removes the fixed term-end sentence and directs the IAOC and Trust to meet near or during the first annual IETF meeting and select chairs first.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7691 updates RFC 4071 and was obsoleted by RFC 8711.

today: RFC 7691 was obsoleted by RFC 8711 and updates RFC 4071, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Why the Existing Dates Were Impractical
sections.content: BCP 101 said IAOC terms normally ended at the end of the first IETF meeting of the year. The RFC explains that this timing caused confusion about who could vote or be elected chair during the meeting week, and could affect whether a quorum was available. Similar problems applied to the IETF Trust.
sections.plainLanguage: The old dates made it unclear which members could vote and whether the committee could conduct business. The RFC says the IETF Trust faced similar issues.

sections.title: Meetings and Term Dates
sections.content: RFC 7691 removes the sentence setting term ends at the end of the first IETF meeting. It directs the IAOC and the IETF Trust each to hold a regular meeting close to or during that meeting. Each group selects its chair as the first order of business. The IAOC sets the start and end dates of member terms relative to its meeting, unless the appointing bodies make those determinations.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAOC and Trust meet near the first IETF meeting and choose their chairs first. The IAOC sets its term dates around its meeting, subject to the appointing bodies.

sections.title: What Counts as a Regular Meeting
sections.content: A regular meeting has proper notice and posted minutes. It may be held face-to-face, by teleconference, or through a combination of the two. The RFC says the meeting and term arrangements are intended to provide more practical timing for member transitions.
sections.plainLanguage: A regular meeting requires notice and posted minutes. Members may meet in person, by phone, or in both ways.
